reason: Plan Phase 5, forced-visibility candidate. The copy has never been seen where it was put, so geometry tuning stops here. Construction is Key Quest Markers' complete cGUIObjTexture recipe, field by field: DTI allocator slot 0x20 with the DTI id, 304 zeroed words, constructor main+0xa4f60c, the bar's +0x50/+0x64/+0x74/+0x78, the twelve style setters in Key Quest Markers' order with its values through the two-integer ABI (BlendState=1, ControlPoint=0, FixFrame=0, Mask=0, Priority=2, ReferencePosition=1, ReferenceRotation=1, ReferenceScaleX/Y/Z=3, Reverse=0, SamplerState=0), the Texture id last through main+0xa4faf0, then mTextureRect through main+0xa4fb58 given a pointer to the bar's live four floats. One set of forced values is written at the build and never again: the bar's position pair with 32.0 added to y, the bar's own authored pair as the size (88.0 x 24.0), and opaque magenta 0xFFFF00FF at the four corners, the bar's own 0xff5efaff being yellow in AABBGGRR. The node stays the scissor mask's sibling on the root's chain, drawn after the mask's subtree and outside the scissor; the row's 6-word map and 88-byte 11-record draw block are r51's. Nothing writes the node per frame: write_dim and the fill copy log line are deleted. The mask's enter now reads the copy's and the bar's own state back before any write - the rect at +0xe0, the effective rect at +0xf0, the 16-word matrix at +0x10..+0x4c, the position pair and the authored pair - prints it on change at most every 30 update ticks, with the floats as floats, and the cut line's tex= prints floats too. Prediction: a magenta full-length blade 32 units under the sharpness gauge, no pulse; the read-back that confirms it is pos=284.0 256.0, size=88.0 24.0, a rect 88 by 24, the matrix's x row 1.0 and eff= equal to rect=. r44's accepted cut and its 128 px-at-0% / 200 px-at-100% endpoints are unchanged. 23 host fixtures pass; verify PASSED with 33 signature windows, the twelve setter windows Key Quest Markers verifies checked here as well.
runtime_test: NOT RUN. The accepted cut is r44's, accepted on its Eden run of 2026-10-30. Phase 5 attempts on Eden 2026-10-31: r45 froze the game five seconds into both quest launches; r46 refused its copy at stage 52; r47, r48 and r50 ran clean and log the copy built with its texture resolved (records=11, dim=, dim_tex=) with none of it visible in the sharpness gauge, their dim_flags=0x20a0001 being the class constructor's own default (main+0xa4d0d8 writes 0x020a0001 at +0x54); r51 has not been run. Two log readings were corrected on the way here: the words at +0x10c are floats, so the bar's live window is a whole tier band [0, 280, 88, 304] / [0, 304, 88, 328] / [0, 328, 88, 352], not the invented 156..440 slide, and the noisy block in the r47 photo is read as the copy's drawing (inference: its position pair held screen pixels and its window was built from words read as integers, v around 1.13e9). r52 is the visibility test: magenta, full sprite size, 32 units under the gauge, written once, with the copy's own game-computed state printed at the mask's enter. r52 has not been run.

target: MHGU Nintendo Switch 1.4.0; upstream Forge 1.5.1; Eden/Ryujinx. Base game and optional MHGU HD Project.
limitations: r4 has no runtime test; its lines, the 320-sample budget and the absence of any drawing change are static results.
r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r25 has not been run. r24's run drew the gauge from the quest start and lost it at an area change, where a mask kept clipping after its links broke; the disable-on-loss path has no runtime evidence, and a mask inserted into a second area's row has never been observed (r24's log ends 12 s after the transition, gauge HUD absent)
r40 has not been run. Its two defaults are the endpoints the r39 log shows applied (right edge 129 px at 0% and 201 px at 100%), read from the tester's run, not from an r40 run.
r42 has not been run. Its fill comes from the player fields Phase 1 verified and the r41 run's accepted geometry; the per-frame fill has not been seen on screen.
r43 has not been run. 128 px at 0% is proven by the r42 log (the tester dragged the start there); 200 px at 100% is the tester's measurement, and that run's box ended at 201.
The thread that runs the draw walker at main+0xa494a0 is unproven, and the run did not change that: no bl site, stored word or DTI property in main names that entry.

the dim blade appearing in the sharpness gauge: r47 and r48 log the copy built with its texture resolved, and the tester sees no copy there. Their dim_flags=0x20a0001 is the class constructor's default, so it is not evidence that the copy draws; the copy's own game-computed rect, matrix, position and authored pair have never been read back.

The MT `color` word's byte order is unproven, so the dim blade's alpha byte position is an inference. The facts line now prints the bar's four corner colours, so a run pins it next to the colour on screen.

The r44 release bytes are preserved in backups/accepted/modern-sharpness-gauge/r44-before-dim-empty-blade/, runtime UNCHANGED; r45 through r51 are superseded; r52 is a new candidate and carries no distribution approval.

The construction recipe, the texture resolve and the read-back fields are read from the decompiles in work/research-tooling/ghidra-export and Key Quest Markers' accepted record. evidence.manual_summary: r44 ran once on Eden 2026-10-30 (installed NRO matched the packaged payload): 209 fill lines on bar rect 110 38 238 166 with feed=128, three insertions, three links-lost teardowns, no guest exception; the tester reported the cut where r43 put it with the HD Project on, which closed the HD Project question. r45's run (2026-10-31) froze the game: no insertion line on any path, then a guest null read at the gauge's first draw. r46's run (2026-10-31) had no fault and the accepted cut on screen; its line shows the copy was refused: 'records=9 dim=0x0' and 'dim blade not added at stage 52'. r47/r48/r50 ran clean with the copy in the tree and none of it visible in the sharpness gauge; r50's quad line proves the placement (rect 157..200, authored 43 at about 44%) with the window on the tier band axis. r51 and r52 have not been run.
